title: Straight in at the top
question: How many people start on the City payroll in the best-paid twentieth, with no earlier City record, in which departments and in which job classes?
finding: Of 21,675 people who first appear on the payroll between fiscal 2019 and fiscal 2026, 785 (3.6%) started at an hourly rate in the best-paid twentieth of City staff ($239,116 a year or more in fiscal 2026). 477 of them are physicians, dentists and nurses, 121 are in legal classes and 123 in management classes; 670 hold exempt appointments. Outside medicine, the most top-tier entrants are in City Attorney (74), Public Health (48) and District Attorney (35); the most into management classes are in Public Health (29) and Public Utilities Commission (16).
how: City payroll file. The file names employees from fiscal 2017; a person counts as new when the name first appears in fiscal 2019 or later, so two named years show no earlier record. The hourly rate is regular salary divided by hours in the first year’s main job (at least 160 hours), which allows for a part year and leaves out overtime and one-time payments. The threshold is the rate that 95% of City rows with half a year of hours or more fall below, set year by year. Management, medical, nursing and legal are the job families the file itself gives each class. Elected offices, board seats and the Superior Court are left out. Ranked by the number of top-tier entrants outside medicine and nursing.
limits: Hiring a senior person from outside is common for department heads, physicians and attorneys, and 670 of these 785 appointments are of the exempt kind, which the City Charter (section 10.104) excludes from competitive selection. A name new to the file is not always a new employee: someone who left before fiscal 2017, when the file has no names, or who changed name, looks new. The count shows where senior outside hiring concentrates; whether a post was advertised and how the person was chosen is in the job announcement and appointment paperwork.
